clue.text: Case made for mummy's confinement?

parts.note: surface reading: a mother's maternity case, packed ready for going into hospital to give birth
setter's reading: the stone coffin that encloses an embalmed Egyptian body

explanation.walkthrough: Confinement is the old word for the period of giving birth, and mummy is a British word for mother, so the clue first suggests a hospital bag; the mummy is in fact an embalmed corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone coffin, often carved, in which ancient Egyptians placed an embalmed body, is exactly a case that confines a mummy.

clue.text: Team produces unexpected results?

parts.note: a side is a sports team
to effect a change is to bring it about, so effects means produces

explanation.surface: A team's performance throws up surprising outcomes.
explanation.walkthrough: Effects here is the verb (to effect is to cause), not the noun, which is easy to miss because the answer's second word is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondary consequences nobody intended, such as those of a medicine, are called by this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Key books in religious studies: his speciality?

definitions.text: Key books in religious studies: his speciality?

indicators.note: to put something in is to place it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: RI is religious instruction, the British school subject
A is a musical key
B is the abbreviation for book, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Asking which key texts in religious education this man specialises in.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is the British school subject religious instruction. The whole clue doubles as the definition: these key books are exactly what such a scholar studies.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish teacher and scholar of law and scripture is expert in the central sacred texts, which fits the whole clue read as a description.

clue.text: What's fitting for rower from Harvard or Yale we're told?

definitions.text: What's fitting for rower from Harvard

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so a word goes by its sound not its spelling

parts.note: the little word or is said just like the blade a rower pulls
Yale is a well-known brand of lock

explanation.surface: Asking what equipment suits a rower from one of the great American university crews.
explanation.walkthrough: Harvard and Yale look like a pair of rival universities, but Harvard only marks the American word, and Yale is the lock brand. The British say rowlock.
explanation.definitionFit: The swivelling fitting on a boat's side that holds a rower's blade is called this in American English.

clue.text: Leader deceived about office finally

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to have someone is to fool them, so had means deceived

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of office

explanation.surface: A boss who was tricked about the office.
explanation.walkthrough: Had for deceived is colloquial: you have been had when you have been conned.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a school, department or organisation is commonly called its head.

clue.text: Taxonomic groups split into individuals of similar age

parts.note: genera are the ranks of classification above species

indicators.note: something split is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Biological categories being divided up into groups of the same age.
explanation.walkthrough: Into looks like a joining word, but it is the four letters that get split.
explanation.definitionFit: All the people born and living at about the same time form one cohort, such as the baby-boomer cohort.

clue.text: Literary genre almost fits iconic scene in novel format

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
a novel format is a new arrangement, so the letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: the word without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A literary genre that almost suits a famous scene adapted as a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like part of the literary surface, but with format it says the letters take a new shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories of imagined futures, space travel and invented technology make up a well-known category of fiction writing.

clue.text: Land using stone passage we hear

explanation.walkthrough: Land looks like a verb in the surface; it is the noun, a country.

clue.text: Anagram aligns with edges of eligible fodder

indicators.note: the setter names the device outright, a cheeky bit of honesty in the surface

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outer letters, so only first and last are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of eligible

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter describing an anagram that lines up with suitable material for a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: Fodder is crossword jargon for the letters an anagram uses, so the surface reads as setter talk; here it is the definition, animal feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass or other green crops stored and fermented in a silo to feed livestock in winter is another name for silage.

clue.text: Some number subtracted from lower number

explanation.surface: A sum about subtracting one number from a smaller one.
explanation.walkthrough: The final number is read as numb-er, something that numbs, not a figure; nether is an old word for lower.

clue.text: Killer returned and cut down European in citadel

clue.text: Becoming fairly good

clue.text: Person no longer having to accommodate issue?

clue.text: Engineer reminds open branch to get guard dog

clue.text: Conservative member of the House of Lords rebuffed toady

clue.text: Journalist having something to learn by holding papers back

clue.text: Criticise manoeuvre moving ring in glittering array

clue.text: Game associated with US includes quiet period of heightened activity

clue.text: Large settlement of rank furthers claims

clue.text: A ridiculous ban on women's lib includes old lady and elusive creature

clue.text: Repeatedly bomb China

clue.text: One involved in endless task that is boring vocal group

clue.text: Trap left criminal corporation without millions

clue.text: Get ready to put TV channels into effect?

TV stations are broadcasting channels

clue.text: Careless fielders at cover dropping ball

clue.text: Present that's small: maybe a foot?

clue.text: Secures Greek fruit

clue.text: Committee introduces conclusion in dutiful summary

the end is the conclusion

explanation.walkthrough: Summary is the adjective (a summary account), not the noun.

clue.text: Host introducing song with welcome for musician

clue.text: Lay to rest strange cases for one new breach in rules?

clue.text: Bankrupt's case undoubtedly involves owing money

explanation.surface: An older man's attractiveness baffles a woman at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Of looks like a joining word attaching sex appeal to older men, but its O starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal word means vigour or energy, and especially physical attractiveness or glamour.

clue.text: Aide is not upset about newspaper's transfer of ownership

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a national is a newspaper sold across the whole country

explanation.surface: An assistant is unhappy about the newspaper being sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: A national is a British paper sold nationwide, such as The Times. Upset reads as distressed but scrambles the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling off a state-owned industry to private buyers moves who owns it, which is privatisation.

clue.text: Very bright child reportedly drowned

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word counts for its sound

parts.note: a son is a child
drowned can mean soaked through

explanation.surface: A clever youngster was said to have drowned.
explanation.walkthrough: Very bright child reads as a gifted youngster, but bright is the definition and the child is a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A place bathed in strong sunshine is brilliantly lit, as with a sunny beach.

clue.text: Union member backing protest about time and space for rest breaks?

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so this piece comes last
about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: a sit-in is a protest occupation
T is the abbreviation for time
a groom is one partner in a marriage union

explanation.surface: A trade unionist supports a protest over hours and a room for breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Union member suggests a trade unionist, but it is a bridegroom in a marriage. Rest breaks hints at sitting down rather than tea breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge in a home is where people sit and relax, so it is a room for resting.
